newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Chimimport eyes Russian chemical market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Chimimport eyes Russian chemical market.

text.p: Bulgarian chemical and oil trading company Chimimport plans to expand its position on the Russian chemical products market, its general director said on Thursday.
Belo Belov said that 60 percent of Chimimport's chemical products trade was currently on the Russian market.
"Chimimport has strong ties with Russia and Ukraine and is committed to seizing new opportunities and developing its presence in the rising markets of Russia and former Soviet republics," Belov said.
Chimimport, established as a state foreign trade organisation in 1947, became a joint stock company in 1994 after its management team bought 78.7 percent of the shares for $21 million.
The remaining 21.3 percent of shares are owned by the Bulgarian Trade Ministry, which has offered them to Chimimport's management for $3 million, a price Belov said was too high.
"We are interested in buying the remaining shares for a reasonable price but not for $3 million," he told a news conference.
The company's net profit was 235 million levs ($150,000) in 1996 against 549 million levs in 1995, the first year in which it was managed as a private company, said accountant Sasho Karagiozov.

Chimimport was among the companies approved by the United Nations to purchase Iraqi crude under the U.N. approved oil-for-food deal. "We have already received some 900,000 tonnes out of the approved one million tonnes," Belov said.

Chimimport, which has nine subsidiaries in Europe and three in Bulgaria, plans to develop the production of its Semperdur subsidiary in Vienna, producing plastic and aluminium window frames under licence from Austria's Shuco, Belov said. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561 ($ = 1565 Bulgarian Levs)
